title: Hadith on World and Hereafter Comparison
summary: The hadith compares the insignificance of worldly life to the vastness of the hereafter.
translation: There is a narration from Sahih Muslim in which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) illustrated the comparison between this world and the hereafter. He indicated that by Allah, in comparison to the hereafter, this world is like a situation where someone among you dips their ring into the sea and then observes what the ring brings back. The meaning of this hadith is that if someone dips their ring into the sea and pulls it out, they would see that it merely comes out with a single drop or a little bit of water. Thus, one should understand that the duration and pleasures of this world are as insignificant and inferior to the time and delights of the hereafter as the water clinging to the ring is to the entire sea. In fact, this example is merely to help people understand, otherwise there is no real comparison between the finite and the infinite. The infinite cannot truly be compared to the finite, just as the small drop of water, despite its insignificance and brief existence, still holds some relation to the sea. However, the world holds even less relation to the hereafter than to the sea and water. Therefore, Hazrat Mulla Ali Qari (may Allah have mercy on him) explains that one should not be arrogant about the fleeting pleasures and comforts of this world, nor should they complain about its hardships and troubles. Instead, according to the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), one should remember that true life is the life of the hereafter, saying, 'O Allah, there is no real life except the life of the hereafter.' Hence, one should always keep the hereafter in mind and understand at all times that this world is merely a farm for the hereafter and that life here is just a moment. Therefore, rather than wasting this moment, one should spend it in the remembrance of Allah, seeking His pleasure, worship, and good behavior towards people. This is the greatest wisdom and understanding. Thus, a person should always prioritize the hereafter and focus on establishing, improving, and earning their worldly life in the perspective of the hereafter.
